source_sections: S9.1 Purpose and relationship to ISO 19650
S9.2 Digital ecosystem and tool authority
core_principles: Tools serve governance; tools do not define governance.
Each tool/domain must have explicit authority boundaries.
Automation is an execution layer, not an authority layer.
Automation must be documented, repeatable, auditable and aligned with standards and registries.
New tools require declared authority, governed integration and preserved information integrity.
Non-authoritative tools may consume or transform information but may not silently become sources of truth.
migration_observations: S9 should remain tool-aware but not tool-instructional; exact execution belongs in workflows/instructions/configuration.
The Automation Registry and Tool Authority Matrix are real governance requirements but not yet concrete source data sets.
Existing repository role ROLE-TOOL-AUTHORITY-001 and downstream automation references can consume S9 but do not replace the missing S9 parent standard.
Cross-tool specializations should inherit S9 authority rather than become independent competing authority models.

provenance.migration_note: Direct source inventory only; no canonical S9 content promoted by this file.
